items.title: Barb Lee, Elora-Fergus Arts Council introduced the work of local artist
notes: Grayce Perry.

Grayce Perry outlined her work focusing on paper collage and spoke of her process to work in series, such as the gateway series and the bubble series. She also noted the Elora Fergus Spring Open Studio Tour May 31 to June 1 from 10 -5 pm.

items.title: County Council Report
notes: Diane Ballantyne, County Councillor Ward 6 provided an overview of various County projects and initiatives such as the Green Legacy tree giveaway, the Multicultural Festival, the inclusion of a Children’s section at the museum, automated speed enforcement, road and intersection improvements underway, the Elora Transfer Station renovations and the $10 minimum fee, and upcoming changes to the recycling program.

items.title: Marko Cirovic, Director of Sector Engagement, IESO re: item 11.1
notes: Information Report - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility)

M. Cirovic indicated the IESO aims to provide a fact-based view of the province’s growing need for electricity and the important role securing new electricity infrastructure plays in ensuring Ontario continues to have a reliable, affordable and sustainable electricity system today and in the future. He indicated the IESO maintains reliability by overseeing the operation of the grid in real time – 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and conducts ongoing planning and procurement processes to ensure Ontario’s electricity system has the infrastructure and tools in place to meet our needs 20-years into the future. M. Cirovic stated the demand for electricity in Ontario is expected to increase 75 per cent by 2050.

M. Cirovic responded to questions regarding the demand for electricity in Ontario, potential to facilitate the installation of home car chargers, the Independent Electricity System Operator’s (IESO) Long-Term One (LT1) procurement process, and the extent of the incentives and penalties.

items.title: Andrew Thiele, Energy Storage Canada re: item 11.1 Information Report
notes: - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility)

A. Thiele indicated Energy Storage Canada is a non profit organization and a national trade association. They represent energy storage developers from coast to coast to ensure a greener more affordable grid. They are supportive of the Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System project advancing energy storages solutions, providing flexible energy and reducing peak demand costs.

items.title: Pierre Chauvin, Agent for the Applicant, MHBC re: item 11.1 Information
notes: Report - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) provided an overview of the changes and improvements to the site plan, including a greater setback, landscaping, noise wall and storm water management pond and the agricultural rehabilitation plan.

items.title: Ondrej Benjik, Aypa Power Canada re: item 11.1 Information Report -
notes: RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) noted Aypa Power Canada was founded in Ontario in 2016 with headquarters in Toronto. He outlined details on servicing Canada’s grid, economy & workforce by strengthening Energy Independence, investing in a strong Canadian supply chain and powering local jobs. He provided details and an update on the Elora BESS project and highlighted the rigorous site selection process.

Ondrej Benjik, Aypa Power Canada responded to questions regarding the origin of the company, the location of the headquarter buildings throughout the US and Canada, and the community outreach undertaken.

items.title: Jeff Roy, Canadian Solar re: item 11.1 Information Report - RZ05/24,
notes: 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) appeared in support of the proposal. Canadian Solar serves as the manufacturer and system integrator for the project. He explained the systems are engineered to the highest safety standards making them a world leader in clean energy, rooted in Canada and home to 220 employees. He noted their systems utilize lithium iron phosphate chemistry, recognized for their safety and reliability.

items.title: Douglas Crossman, Valard Construction re: item 11.1 Information
notes: Report - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) provided an overview of the Canadian company, emphasizing on safety, local investment and reliability in delivering critical infrastructure across Canada.
D. Crossman responded to questions regarding 200 employees to be involved in the Aypa Power project and the commitment to maximizing local goods and service.

items.title: Bishoy N. Awad, Fire & Risk Alliance re: item 11.1 Information Report -
notes: RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) provided an overview of the company, a leader in providing fire protection solutions. He provided a high level overview of the required standards and codes for battery storage systems and responded to a question regarding the headquarters for the company.

items.title: Deborah Whale, Grand River Agricultural Society re: item 11.1
notes: Information Report - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) appeared in support of the project. She noted farmers in the area have increasing demands for energy that is clean, green and non-polluting. As their operations grow so does the demand for more complex technology, electronic vehicles and robotics to remain competitive.

items.title: Marina Sampson, McCarthy Tétrault LLP, appearing on behalf of Aypa
notes: Power re: item 11.1 Information Report - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol (Aypa Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility) provided an opinion on the recent Provincial procurement restriction policy enacted in response to the US tariffs. She offered three points on the policy, (1) the policy only applies to procurements, (2) the policy applies to new procurements and (3) the policy does not apply to and doesn’t bind the Township of Centre Wellington.
M. Sampson responded to questions regarding the law firm’s affiliation with Blackstone and the current trade environment.
Mayor Watters called for a 7 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 7:47 pm.
